summary: Hexagonal wooden screw-pile light in Tangier Sound, Maryland, lit 1892. Its house came down in 1964 and a steel tower replaced it.

structures.note: Erected on a battery house on the old screw-pile foundation

access.note: Not open to the public (Society record).

events.note: Board recommends a screw-pile light and fog signal, about $25,000, to replace the washed-away Clay Island light
Congress appropriates $25,000; borings made at the shoal
Metal-work proposals in January, contract in February; superstructure begun in April at the Lazaretto depot, Baltimore
Governor of Maryland signs application relinquishing jurisdiction over the site (December)
Superstructure towed to site 3 June and erected in June
Thomas T. Cole transferred from Clay Island and appointed keeper
Light dark for more than a week while navigation was blocked (Snow Hill paper, February)
New model fourth-order lamps installed; roof, gutters and downspouts renewed
Soundings made around the light; various repairs
Keeper W. C. Carew rescued two men in a small skiff, 2 to 8 February, after they were caught in drift ice
Automatic light on a skeletal tower erected on a battery house

corrections.current: tower, screwpile, wood, built 1892, 13.4 m, standing
corrections.proposed: steel skeletal tower on a battery house on the screw-pile foundation, built 1964; 1892 wooden house removed 1964
corrections.why: The Society's record and LighthouseFriends say the wooden house was removed in 1964 and a steel skeletal tower erected on a battery house. Whether that tower stands today is not settled by the sources read.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record gives deactivation in 1964 and a 2022 entry (from Rowlett's directory, not checked here). The Society's record and LighthouseFriends give 1964 as the year of discontinuance and removal. The story uses 1964.
LighthouseFriends dates automation to 1950, the year the archive's last principal keeper's stint ends. The 1964 date is the house's removal, not automation.

notes_for_editor: Roster: 20 archive lines, matched by name and position (0.17 km), copied as printed; no duplicates. Carew's principal stint: archive 1904-1920; LighthouseFriends 1904-1933. The story says 1920 as the archive's end date only through the roster, and does not state the LighthouseFriends end date. The 1918 Bulletin text (printed p. 20) is badly OCR'd and is not quoted; the rescue is cited to LighthouseFriends, the Chesapeake timeline and the index. 'Capt. Cole' in the 1893 Snow Hill paper is linked to Thomas T. Cole by the 1892 Annapolis item (transfer and appointment to this station) and the roster; that link is a source's, not a shared name alone. Daniel Asbury White: the 1922 obituary names him as a keeper at Shark's Fin and Great Shoal; the archive has him as first assistant at both. Linked as other_stations on both stations' lines, cited to the obituary. William H. Davis (1926 obituary): helped build Sharkfin Shoal as a carpenter of the field party; later keeper of the Lazaretto depot. Not on this roster; mentioned in the prose only. Gordy Z. Parks and Raymond C. Peters are on this station's roster and the Great Shoals roster with the same archive person slug; the story notes the Great Shoals stints from the Great Shoals record. Record corrections: structure (1892 wooden house removed 1964; the record says standing). Focal height 13.5 m in the record vs 44 ft (13.4 m) in USLHS and LighthouseFriends: a small difference, not corrected. The record's light characteristic (Fl W 4s) and range (7.0 nm) are not confirmed by any source read here and are not in facts. Record deactivation 2022 (Rowlett's) is not checked here. Position: record (OSM) 38.202164, -75.986741 vs LighthouseFriends 38.202169, -75.986771: the same place within a few metres. Wikipedia places the light at the mouth of the Nanticoke River; LighthouseFriends and the Annapolis papers place it in Tangier Sound. Wikipedia used for leads only. Chesapeake timeline 1947: a keeper of this station (Palmquist, per the timeline) and another keeper, both men, died when a station boat caught fire at Hooper Strait Lighthouse (Daily Times, Salisbury, 23 Dec 1947, not checked). It happened at Hooper Strait, not here, and is not in the story. Lighthouse Board reports for the 1880s (1887 to 1890 recommendations and appropriations) are not in the local corpus (lhb covers 1891-1901); those facts come from LighthouseFriends's transcription and are cited to it. The Board's 1893 report (Jessamine employed on Sharkfin construction) was not used. The USCG Historian's page is blocked (403); not used. Newspapers: three searches; three pages read. Sources for the 1918 rescue are the index, LighthouseFriends and the timeline. No women keepers or keepers' families are named in the sources read. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the Snow Hill paper's word that Cole 'was either very sick or had perished from cold and hunger' is taken from OCR where the word reads 'per islicd'; the page image was not checked. The 1926 obituary is cited to PDF p. 24 (verified). Index p. 93 for the 1891-92 report is read from an OCR index entry ('1 93'); scan page 444 confirmed. The 1922 obituary lists Thomas' Point as a third light; the story now says so. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the regulations sentence after the Snow Hill quotation was dropped because the cached OCR ('pill up the lights') does not support a reading of what the keepers were not required to do.
